pr_body:
The LeaderElection logic already cancel the context passed to the OnStartLeading callback when stop leading, so there is no need to add a new context and cancel explicitily.

Add integration tests to assert this logic and avoid regressions in the future.

/kind bug
/kind flake

Fixes #127665

```release-note
NONE
```

/assign @Jefftree @jpbetz @liggitt

issue_context.title: cancel function could be nil in CLE leader election path
issue_context.body:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/124012#discussion_r1777340551

Per https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/leaderelection/leaderelection.go#L210, we could call OnStoppedLeading before OnStartedLeading gets called leading to a nil cancel function. We should check the function before calling it.

/sig api-machinery
/triage accepted

review_comments: um... how is it compatible to no longer cancel the context passed into `run` when OnStoppedLeading triggers?

There is two context here, the one passed as parameter that is the one used in `le.Run(ctx)`, this controls the overall leader elector.

The context here is the one derived from that context in the Run method, that is always canceled after the OnStartedLeading hook is called and the overall context is cancelled or the lease can not renewed

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2fb37e2489133edbbe8f318f920ef3515b0c8d58/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/leaderelection/leaderelection.go#L207-L219

The problem here is that `le.config.Callbacks.OnStoppedLeading()` is always called, even if `OnStartedLeading(ctx)` is never executed, that may cause for the cancelfunction to be nil and panic, see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127675#discussion_r1780017493

Since the goal is to stop the run() function, the integration test ensure that it is always cancelled , just the overall context is cancelled or the lease can not be renewed

hey @liggitt !  I used to think that `OnStoppedLeading` would definitely be called after `OnStartedLeading`. However, after reviewing the code, it seems that this is not the case. I initially wanted to modify this logic in the PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127675 , but after discussion https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127675#discussion_r1780059887 , it seems that maintaining the original code would be better because this code has been around for a long time, and making sudden changes might introduce unforeseen issues. Therefore, we decided to update the comments https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127743 to make the code logic clearer for users, avoiding potential problems.
Will both be called at most once, or is it possible to start/stop/start/stop?

> Will both be called at most once, or is it possible to start/stop/start/stop?

The changes in this PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127675  are intended to achieve the method you mentioned. However, as discussed above, there may be maintenance impacts.
The code logic that has not been changed now: Regardless of whether the OnStartedLeading method is called, the OnStoppedLeading method will always be called.
heh, yeah, kind of have this template for integration tests that I need to update
I'm not sure we should add logging into this method in code paths we expect to execute normally
is OnStartedLeading supposed to be able to be called multiple times? if it is, is it expected to be paired 1:1 with calls to OnStoppedLeading?

Checking the code it seems it is only called once https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127737/files/fff04976265b0186000191a5be76c940e5bce3cf#r1781331967

Since this function does not return errors, I think we need logs to be able to understand the state for troubleshooting

Leader transitions should be rare (generally only on failure conditions or restarts/upgrades) so I'm in favor of keeping the log for troubleshooting.

You're right that OnStartedLeading and OnStoppedLeading are called once max, though it should be possible for an apiserver to acquire leader, release it, and acquire the leader again. The code currently doesn't allow reacquiring after release and is a bug which I will submit a fix for https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/127783 but that's orthogonal to the panic issue.

> The code currently doesn't allow reacquiring after release and is a bug which I will submit a fix for #127783 but that's orthogonal to the panic issue.

It's not really orthogonal ... OnStoppedLeading is using a variable set by OnStartedLeading... if they can be called concurrently or repeatedly, the current variable sharing is unsafe (which can cause a panic, a data race, or a hung context)
Callbacks can not be called concurrently checking the code ... and now it seems you need to `Run()` again once the leadership is lost

> Callbacks can not be called concurrently checking the code

I'm... not sure that's true... we call OnStartedLeading in a goroutine so it *could* be concurrent with OnStoppedLeading() (but I agree it's unlikely to be):

```
go le.config.Callbacks.OnStartedLeading(ctx)
```

a simple nil check on `ctx` with a TODO to resolve concurrency issues and multi-call issues in a follow-up should resolve the test flake and not make things worse, and be a smaller change to reason about
